Grateful for the opportunity to join colleagues at @UNDPChina country office to to discuss how our new UNDP Strategic Plan 2026–2029 puts sustainable energy at the center of development; not just as an enabler, but as a strategic lever for shifting the development curve itself. 

China’s experience shows why this matters. With 47% of global wind & solar; 20M EVs (half the global fleet); and having already achieved its 2030 renewables target six years early, China is proving that transitions can be nationally transformative and globally catalytic. But ultimately, this is not only about megawatts; it is about people, communities and systems for shared prosperity. 

In our dialogue, I shared three priorities for deepening China’s leadership and expanding shared progress: 

🔹 South–South and triangular cooperation
With 25 regional projects totaling 12 GW of new capacity worth $5B under the Shanghai Cooperation Organization, and partnerships across Africa, Asia and the Pacific, China is extending its leadership. The next step is moving from projects to scalable solutions grounded in governance, safeguards and inclusion. 

🔹 Digital, data & AI for energy systems
With grid investment projected at $100B annually and data center demand set to nearly double to 945 TWh by 2030, China is pioneering AI forecasting, digital twins and open data. Embedding these innovations into just transition frameworks is essential to ensure they deliver inclusive benefits 

🔹 Energy as a lever for human development 
As set out in the new Strategic Plan, success will not be measured only in megawatts, but in human outcomes: schools and clinics with reliable power; farmers with modern tools; households with clean cooking; and communities with greater resilience to crisis. 

At UNDP we are proud to work alongside China and global partners to connect innovation with governance, finance, and inclusion. A just energy transition is not only a national achievement – it's a shared global responsibility. The real challenge is not how fast we expand renewables, but how effectively we connect them to the people who need them most.
